column3: Shows that concealed planning remains within encompassing divine knowledge, against public-facing display.
Extends reckless self-display into the reversal and emptying of its settled outcome.
Directly develops blocking the way through its distortion before others.
Adds a material-interest pattern that turns gain into public obstruction of the way.
The immediate sequel exposes boastful confidence as adorned, unstable, and abandoned at encounter.
Only supplies a contrast-route boundary, without a usable addition here.
Offers a contrasting departure governed by fear of death rather than public display.
Nearby condemnation of persistent disbelief adds little to the focus's conduct and motive.
Links inadequate grasp and rejection to accountable action under comprehensive knowledge.
Sets division and disagreement after clear signs as a communal contrary pattern.
The bare rejection-and-disobedience notice adds no distinct interpretive element.
Develops encompassing divine governance beyond actors' own reach.
Contrasts battlefield regret and fatalistic claims with divine knowledge of what people do.
The immediate continuation supplies a contrary reading of trust against hostile judgment of the faithful.
Shows declared collective backing failing at the point of actual departure and combat.
Provides a departure from homes oriented to divine favor and support rather than display.

Intensifies the encompassing-knowledge dimension through complete accounting and custody.
Supplies the nearby warning that claimed hearing may fail to become real reception.
Offers loss of a path and support, but without a close link to the focus's motive or public action.
Adds the possibility that deeds lose standing under final evaluation despite apparent activity.

Places cessation of disorder and divine seeing of deeds within the same surah's conflict frame.
Only weakly contrasts controlled visibility of effort with self-directed display.
Connects worldly preference, distortion, and obstruction of the way as a settled orientation.

Directly isolates doing things for others' sight as a durable parallel to the focus's public display.
Adds self-forgetfulness following forgetfulness of God as an inward consequence.

Contrasts public communal responsibility for good and against wrong with obstructive conduct.
Adds deceptive self-protection that becomes an organized barrier to others' movement on the way.
The call to worship and avoid corruption has no sufficiently specific addition here.
Frames apparent distance from consequence as already enclosed by it.
Offers expulsion for confession and divinely supported defense as a contrasting kind of departure.
The nearby punishment notice adds consequence but not an interpretive connection to the focus.
Cowardice in danger and harsh speech afterward weakly contrast with genuine commitment.
Brings hidden disbelief beneath divine knowledge, qualifying outward claims.
Generic punishment patterns add little after the earlier consequence cards.
Provides a specific public-display pattern in giving, joined to an inwardly corrupt companionship.
Connects following desire with diversion from the way, including a leadership and judgment setting.
Divine reinforcement is relevant battle context but is already more fully developed nearby.
Shows hidden affiliations being disclosed through enacted commitment rather than profession.
Adds exchange of divine signs for small gain as a public barrier to the way.
A branch-level display resonance is too indirect to carry much weight.
Only contrast evidence is supplied; it is not positive support for the focus reading.
The warning about harming Moses does not materially develop the focus's action or motive.
Immediately attributes reassurance and victory to God, countering self-exalting confidence.
Distinguishes receiving the message from claiming authority over hidden deeds.
Reiterates encompassing knowledge but adds little after the earlier, closer instances.
The sign-display branch remains too indirect for the focus.
Pairs resistance to being diverted from the signs with a continuing call toward the Lord.
Encompassing knowledge of hostile plotting is relevant but redundant at this point.
The immediate military scene shows perception being ordered toward a settled divine outcome.
Its route is contrast-only and does not positively extend the focus.
Exposes outwardly selective commitment while divine awareness remains in view.
Loss of any return-path is only a remote, branch-level relation.
Adds divine presence and sight across all movement, broadening the accountability frame.
Directly depicts participation that would produce disorder and seek fitna within the group.
The immediate prior verse sets stopping and returning as a boundary before the conflict sequence.
Reward for workers is too general to add much to the focus's public-performance concern.
Compactly reinforces that no direction lies outside the encompassing divine relation.
Its branch associations are remote from the focus's display, obstruction, and accountability cluster.
Adds preservation rather than loss of rightly oriented deeds under divine evaluation.
Sets migration, injury, fighting, and death within a rewarded rather than performative horizon.
Immediately prepares the focus by naming fear and internal dispute that altered perception would trigger.
Joins personal turning away with a repeated public obstruction of the way.
Wrongdoing and illicit gain are too general after more direct obstruction cards.
The immediate aftermath locates hostile conduct within severe consequence.
Sharpens the risk that seemingly productive deeds may be the deepest loss.
Contrasts mere exposure to speech with receptive understanding and response.
The branch-level recoil of harm is too indirect to outweigh the missing direct link.
Patiently awaiting another's movement is only a distant contrast to the focus's departure.
Treats doubt as occurring within, rather than outside, a comprehensive divine relation.
General recompense for action is now largely redundant.
The encompassing-punishment phrase is insufficiently specific to the focus.
Exposes the contradiction between seeking visible standing and denying accountable visibility.
The isolated idol reference offers no usable connection.
Knowledge of deeds is present but the food-and-work instruction is not a close extension.
Gives a concrete pattern of occupying routes, restricting access, and bending the way.
Its request for exit is a remote movement parallel without the focus's public or obstructive dimension.
Directly pairs public-facing ritual with inward reluctance, exposing the split behind display.
Testing through worldly adornment and action is a broad, now redundant accountability parallel.
Its ethical instruction around oaths and reconciliation has only an indirect relation.
Collective contribution and protection form a remote movement-and-exit resonance.
Earlier in the surah directly joins spending to obstruction of the way and its eventual reversal.
Fearful refusal to enter is only a limited contrary movement pattern.
Sets a boundary against aligning with wrongdoers and relying on false support.
Develops misdirection that is falsely assessed as guidance, not merely an externally closed path.
Directly joins rejection and obstruction of the way to the undoing of deeds.
Adds differentiated, fully returned outcomes for deliberate deeds.
Supplies an ethical boundary: prior obstruction must not become transgression, while cooperation remains ordered to good.
Divine knowledge and authority are too general here to advance the focus further.
The closing divine sight of deeds is not enough to connect this domestic ruling to the focus.
Directly denies that group wishes or identity claims can substitute for accountable action.
A battle scene of self-concern, concealment, and divine testing offers a useful contrary posture.
The sign of Moses' hand has no meaningful connection to the focus.
The bare command to fear God and obey adds no distinct evidence.
The secure, unexpelled condition is too remote from the focus.
Destruction for wrongdoing is a generic consequence with no close link.
Pride followed by lowering is a distant contrary trajectory, without a direct route to the focus.
Uses the same encompassing relation to deny that opponents stand outside divine reach.
Names obstruction of the way alongside grave religious aggression.
Directly tests public-facing expenditure against an inwardly void act, making it a central display parallel.
Makes hidden and exposed inner content equally subject to divine knowledge.
Provides an immediate battlefield departure from home ordered toward believers' positions rather than display.
Adds a near-battle moment of faltering answered by reliance on God.
Supplies self-protective speech and withdrawal in a battle setting as a contrary posture.
Distinguishes migration undertaken toward God and the Messenger from the focus's self-directed exit.
Reinforces that all things are within divine encompassing knowledge.
Contrasts fear of public blame with committed striving in the way.
Joins what is concealed and made public to knowledge of what people earn.
States comprehensive divine knowledge as the answer to fear and disputation.
Directly combines turning people from the way with seeking its crookedness.
Connects a return-or-refusal conflict to comprehensive divine knowledge.
Supplies the immediate command governing conduct when forces meet.
Defines the boundary between tactical movement and blameworthy turning away in battle.
Places responsive hearing under a life-giving summons and the gathering of all to God.
Warns that disorder can extend beyond its immediate wrongdoers, sharpening the public stakes.
Gives the closest positive counterpart: firmness, remembrance, and hoped success at encounter.
Gives the closest contrary instruction against dispute, loss of courage, and dissipation of force.
Relates consequence to a community's alteration of its own condition.
Adds a battle case in which confidence in one's numbers proves of no avail.
Contrasts attachment to near interests with mobilization in the way.
Makes refusal to mobilize a communal and consequential failure.
Commands mobilization across conditions and striving with wealth and selves.
Exposes an excuse pattern that avoids costly participation.
Contrasts genuine belief with requests for exemption from striving.
Directly treats preparation as evidence of an intended departure, and withholding as divine restraint.
Names an earlier attempt to create disorder and overturn the matter before truth prevailed.
Adds reluctant ritual and reluctant expenditure as an inward qualification of outward religious action.
Supplies complacent refusal to go out as a contrary military disposition.
Directly places human action under divine seeing as well as communal disclosure.
Denies that concealment can hide inward content from divine knowledge.
Makes secrecy and publicity equally exposed to divine knowledge.
Links deceptive oath-taking to slipping, harm, and having obstructed the way.
Uses the same encompassing relation for humanity as a whole, widening the focus's horizon.
Sets right action and unalloyed devotion as a counterpoint to seeking human regard.
Adds the collapse of apparently substantial deeds at final encounter and reckoning.
Explicitly removes any distinction between concealing and exposing what is within.
Provides the direct counter-principle of devotion purified for God.
Restates exclusive, purified devotion as the governing orientation of worship.
Concentrates the same exclusive devotion in the speaker's declared practice.
Combines disbelief, obstruction of the way, and opposition after guidance has become clear.
Joins dying in disbelief with persistent obstruction of the way.
Extends divine knowledge to every private conference and total company.
Challenges the gap between public assertion and enacted conduct.
Intensifies the moral gravity of saying what one does not do.
Provides disciplined, ordered striving as a positive counterpart to boastful and divisive movement.
Defines sincere belief through striving with wealth and selves rather than public display.
Makes the concealed and public alike known, including what hearts contain.
Directly states that divine knowledge encompasses everything.
Equates secrecy and publicity before the knower of inward reality.
Provides an act of giving explicitly detached from return, thanks, and human recognition.
States purified devotion as the core corrective to mixed or public-facing motive.
Extends the existing display parallel to the warned religious performers.
Adds heedlessness within the very practice that is then marked by display.
Completes the display passage with refusal of ordinary aid, testing its outward form by social effect.
